//: Run with `npm run mutate`. Deliberately NOT wired into the guardrails commit gate — `stryker` stays `off` in guardrails.config.json. It is a tool you point at something, not a check that runs on every commit: the command runner below executes the whole test suite once per mutant, which is minutes, and mutation testing pays on pure logic rather than on the I/O that most of this codebase is.
//testRunner: `command`, not `vitest`. @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner spawns its own vitest, which lacks the workers pool's module rules and dies on a binary fixture: `Failed to parse source for import analysis ... the .bin file format`.
//commandRunner: The whole suite, on purpose. The command runner runs one fixed command, so pointing it at a subset means any mutant in a file that subset does not cover survives — and the file then reports 0.00, which reads as a finding and is a configuration error. Measured: ~11s per mutant this way (10 mutants, 109s, concurrency 4) against ~0.6s when the command is narrowed to the covering tests. The safe number is the slow one, so narrow `mutate` rather than `command` — scope it to the file you are working on. `incremental` below means the second run only re-tests what changed.
//mutate: `src/lib` only. These are the pure modules — codecs, contracts, normalisation, the thermal tables. Everything else is D1, R2, queues and TanStack, where a surviving mutant usually means `this line talks to a binding the test replaced`, not `this line is untested`.
